header.author: Book of the Dead
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:egy:tla:tb:pturin-museo-egizio-1791-tb-114-165:translit, from the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (2018), in Simon Schweitzer's AED-TEI (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.T1.11: The lines appear to be captions. Foremost of the God's Booth (ḫnt,j-zḥ-nṯr) is an epithet of Anubis. T1.14: ꜥḥꜥ 'position, standing', perhaps the upright of the balance. T1.15: mḥ 'fill' or 'hold'. Hesret is the necropolis of Hermopolis. Shay, Renenet and Meskhenet are deities of fate, nourishment and birth. The Devourer (ꜥm,tt) is Ammit. Igeret is a name of the necropolis.
notes.T1.7: Wennefer is an epithet of Osiris. Imhet (jmḥ,t) is a region of the netherworld.
notes.130.111: bz štꜣ, 'secret introduction', perhaps 'initiation'. ꜥḥ,t is unclear, perhaps a chamber or palace. The king's name Semti (Zm,tj) is queried by the editor; perhaps Den of the First Dynasty.
notes.133.38: nb!! is marked corrupt. m jti̯ =k m zꜣ =k is probably 'not even your father or your son'; it could also mean they are excepted with you.
notes.148.10: 148.11: ḏi̯ =f, 'he/it causes'; m šꜣ,w, here 'by fate', is uncertain. 148.15: jr,t is marked corrupt. 148.18: ky-ḏd introduces a variant reading.
notes.163.2: 163.2: wnm bꜣ.pl is 'the Eater of bas', a demon (n,tj 'who' is singular); dnm, here 'worms', is uncertain. Irheb, Herty, Remen, Senhaqereg and Senhaperegen are unidentified, foreign-sounding names. 163.5: zꜣ 'protection' or 'son'. 163.7: dp 'taste', perhaps 'consume'.
notes.163.34: 163.34: ḫnw taken as 'troublemaker, disturbance'. 163.35 is obscure: kꜣy perhaps 'the high one' (qꜣy); ḏrt is 'hand' but could also be 'kite'. 163.36: kfꜣ uncertain ('uncover, despoil'); swꜣw, 'passing', taken as going about the land. 163.37: dm 'pierce', or 'pronounce' (his name). 163.40: qnby taken as qnbt, the court of magistrates.
notes.164.28: jrw 'figure, form' is marked doubtful in the edition. Payet (Pꜥyt) is perhaps pꜥt 'humankind', as in 164.32, i.e. a human face; Nerau (Nrjw) is perhaps the vulture (nrw). ꜥnd is unidentified, perhaps for ꜥntjw (myrrh); ryt taken as pigment or ink; pry, a strip or band(?) of the linen, is uncertain.

nodes.text: Book for entering the Hall of the Two Truths, separating a man from the wrongs he has done, to see the faces of the gods.
Words to be spoken: Hail to you, lords of the Two Truths!
Hail to you, great god, lord of the Two Truths!

The secret of the Duat, a secret initiation(?) in the necropolis, found in the *ꜥḥt* of the Great Mansion under the Majesty of the King of Upper and Lower Egypt Semti(?), justified, as a find in the cavern of the mountain, which Horus made for his father Osiris-Wennefer, justified.
Do not perform it for anyone at all except yourself, be it your father or your son.
No one at all is to be allowed to see [it] except the king and the lector priest.
Then he will be like one of them.
It lets [him] know what will happen to him by fate(?).
This book is a secret, truly, truly.
No other anywhere shall ever know [it];
it is not to be told to any people,
nor repeated to an eye(?),
nor heard by an ear,
nor shown to anyone except him and the one who taught him.
Do not be talkative; variant: let it be [given] only to yourself and to your confidant.
You shall perform it inside a booth of cloth, set with stars in abundance all over it.
It is a true mystery.

Spell for not letting a man's corpse perish in the necropolis, to rescue him from the Eater of *bas* (souls) who is imprisoned in the Duat, and for not letting his wrongs on earth be raised up against him, for keeping his flesh and his bones sound against worms(?) and every god who does harm in the necropolis, for letting him go out and come down as he wishes, and do everything in his heart without being hindered.
Words spoken by the Osiris [...], justified:
I am the *ba* of the great corpse which rests in Irheb.
He is the protection of the corpse of Herty, the lord of Remen, who rests in the far region of Senhaqereg.
O *ba* whose heart does not tire of rising and setting, whose *ba* rests inside his corpse which rests in Senhaperegen, come to the Osiris [...], justified!
May he rescue him from the savage-faced *bas*, mighty of heart, who seize limbs, from whose mouths a hot blast comes forth to taste(?) the *bas*.
No troublemaker will be raised up against him.
Effective is the hand of the exalted one(?) in him, for ever and ever.
If this book is made on earth, he will not be despoiled(?) by the transgressing messengers who go about the entire land.
He will not be pierced(?).
He will not die by the king's slaughter.
He will not be taken to any prison.
Rather, he will enter the court and come out justified.

Words to be spoken over a figure(?) of Mut having three faces: one with the face of Pakhet, wearing the two plumes; another with the face of Payet(?), wearing the White and Red Crowns; another with the face of Nerau, wearing the two plumes; having a phallus, having two wings, with the claws of a lion.
Drawn in dry *ꜥnd* on fresh incense, and again in pigment(?) on a *pry* of red linen,
with a dwarf standing before her [and] behind her,
his face toward her, wearing the two plumes,
he with arm raised, having two faces, one with the face of a falcon, the other with the face of a human.
Hail to you, Foremost of the West, Wennefer, lord of Abydos!

May you let [me] open the way of darkness, that I may join your followers who are in the Duat, that I may enter and go forth in Rosetau, in the Hall of the Two Truths, that I may pass the Imhet of the Duat.
I have come [...] *ka* (vital force) [...]
Horus
Foremost of the God's Booth, he says:
The heart is exact in its position(?).
The balance is filled with the Osiris [...], justified.
Words spoken by Thoth, lord of Hermopolis, lord of the god's words, great god, foremost of Hesret:
Give him his heart in its place, to the Osiris [...], justified.
Shay
Renenet
Meskhenet
Driving off the enemies by the Devourer, lady of the West, of(?) the West.
Osiris-Wennefer, lord of life, great god, ruler of eternity, chief of Rosetau and Igeret, foremost of the West, great god, lord of Abydos, king of everlastingness.
